title: Capacity Surface Mapper: safe GPU memory budgeting for weights/KV/activations
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Background: As we increase continuous batching density and enable more aggressive KV caching, we observe tail OOMs during mixed-priority traffic surges. Current heuristics reserve a fixed fraction of GPU RAM for a soft headroom band but do not adapt based on request mix or sequence-length distribution. This ticket proposes a Capacity Surface Mapper (CSM): a telemetry-driven component that maps feasible allocations between weights, KV, and activations for each machine class and produces per-node dynamic headroom targets and admission guidance for the runtime.
problem_statement: We need a deterministic, easily-auditable budgeting layer that (1) computes safe weight/KV/activation allocations under mixed workloads, (2) generates per-node headroom SLOs for continuous batching, and (3) exposes simple runtime signals to prevent OOMs while minimizing wasted capacity.
goals: 1) Reduce tail OOM incidents by 80% for mixed batch workloads. 2) Reduce average conservative headroom waste by 20% vs current fixed-fraction policy. 3) Provide clear rollout path and observability to validate safety in production.
non_goals: Model-level quantization or kernel rewrites (handled in other tickets). This ticket focuses on budgeting and signals, not model weight placement changes.
proposal_points: Collect per-machine memory telemetry (free, reserved, kv_size, active_activation_estimate) from runtime agents and aggregate into a nightly candidate surface model.

Fit a Pareto-sweep of feasible allocations: for each candidate request mix (sequence length percentiles, batch size distribution, KV hit rate), compute minimal activation budget that keeps latency targets while bounding eviction probability under a threshold.
Produce three artifacts: (A) per-machine target headroom fraction (B) per-tenant KV soft caps with recommended eviction priority rules (C) admission gating thresholds for continuous batching layer.
Expose a lightweight REST config endpoint and S3 snapshot for the runtime to consume; runtime falls back to current policy if endpoint unreachable.
Add dashboards showing capacity surface contours, historical headroom decisions, and eviction events for audit and rollout validation.
acceptance_criteria: CSM runs daily and writes per-node headroom snapshot to S3 with schema v1
Runtime consumes snapshot and respects headroom targets for at least 2 node classes in canary cluster
Observed reduction in tail OOMs >= 60% in canary over 2 weeks (goal 80% in rollout)
Dashboards present capacity contours and annotated rollout changelog entries
Automated integration test that runs a micro-simulation (synthetic workload mix) and asserts eviction probability < 1% at configured headroom
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (explore & sim): 2w - Telemetry queries + offline micro-simulator that plays request mixes against a parametric memory model. Phase 2 (mapper prototype): 2w - implement CSM service, produce snapshots, simple REST. Phase 3 (runtime integration): 1w - runtime reads snapshot, guards admission, emits metrics. Phase 4 (canary + iterate): 2w - deploy to canary pool, monitor, tune thresholds. Phase 5 (rollout): staged rollout across node classes and regions.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Surface model divergence — mitigated by conservative fallback policy and regular validation against offline simulator
Risk: Snapshot consumption lag causes outdated targets — mitigated by including snapshot timestamp and TTL; runtime ignores >24h old snapshots
Risk: Increased KV churn due to tighter caps — mitigated by gradual caps and recommending eviction priorities that prefer prefetched/non-hot keys
Risk: Metric instrumentation gaps — mitigation: temporary probes and a small sampling flag to trace edge cases
observability_plan: Add Prometheus metrics: csm_snapshot_age_seconds, csm_headroom_target_fraction{node_class}, csm_inferred_feasible_surface_version. Dashboard panels: heatmap of feasible activation budgets vs sequence length percentiles, eviction rate overlay, and a changelog that maps snapshot versions to observed OOM/eviction deltas.
testing_plan: Unit tests for surface solver, CI micro-sim that replays historical 7-day traffic window and validates no regressions, canary synthetic load generator to exercise mixed priorities, post-deploy gradual aggression sweep (10%->50%->100%).
rollout_steps: Deploy CSM service behind feature flag
Run nightly generation for 1 week and compare recommended headroom to existing policy
Enable runtime consumption in canary cluster (10 nodes) with conservative multiplier 1.15
Monitor for 2 weeks: OOM, eviction, latency; adjust multipliers
Gradually reduce multiplier and expand rollout if safe
open_questions: What is the correct risk threshold for eviction probability (1% vs 0.1%) for P0 tenants?
Should the CSM be per-tenant or per-node-class by default? (preferring per-node-class for stability)
How should KV hotness signals be incorporated into eviction priority (LRU vs frequency-weighted)?
